## Summary

The "Brain": a stateless HTTP service that receives `{ pageState, transcript, conversationHistory }` and returns a schema-valid `BrainResponse` — mapping natural speech onto concrete DOM actions with correct field targeting, spoken-format normalisation, and clarification when the request is ambiguous.

Everything here is **inside the server**. No API keys ever reach the browser extension (see C-3 for the edge proxy the extension actually talks to).

## Stack

- Node 20+, TypeScript, `hono` (`@hono/node-server`) — smallest cold start, no decorators, trivially testable with `app.request()`.
- `zod` v3 (same instance as `@vfe/protocol`), `openai` SDK ≥ 4.x.
- Structured Outputs via `zodResponseFormat(BrainResponseSchema, 'brain_response')` and `client.chat.completions.create({ response_format, ... })` with `strict: true` (OpenAI) — or Anthropic tool-use with the JSON schema derived by `zodToJsonSchema`.
- Provider abstraction: `LlmProvider` interface so Groq (llama/gpt-oss), OpenAI (`gpt-4o-mini`), and Anthropic (`claude-haiku`) are swappable via env. Default: `gpt-4o-mini` for cost/latency.

```ts
export interface LlmProvider {
  readonly name: string;
  readonly model: string;
  complete(args: {
    system: string;
    messages: Array<{ role: 'user' | 'assistant'; content: string }>;
    schema: z.ZodTypeAny;
    schemaName: string;
    temperature?: number;
    timeoutMs?: number;
    signal?: AbortSignal;
  }): Promise<{ parsed: unknown; usage: TokenUsage; raw?: string }>;
}
```

## Endpoint contract

`POST /api/process-command`

Request (validated with `ProcessCommandRequestSchema.parse`; 400 + `{ code: 'INVALID_REQUEST', issues }` on failure):

```json
{
  "pageState": { "urlOrAppTitle": "Checkout — Acme", "elements": [ … ], "globalErrors": [] },
  "transcript": "my name is Alice and my email is alice at wonderland dot com",
  "conversationHistory": [{ "role": "user", "text": "…", "at": 1730000000000 }],
  "clientContext": { "client": "extension", "clientVersion": "0.1.0", "protocolVersion": "1.0.0", "locale": "en-US", "timezone": "America/Phoenix" }
}
```

Response 200:

```json
{
  "brainResponse": {
    "thoughtProcess": "User is providing name and email; two text fields matched by label.",
    "spokenFeedback": "Filled in your name and email.",
    "actions": [
      { "action": "FILL", "targetId": "vfe_1", "value": "Alice" },
      { "action": "FILL", "targetId": "vfe_2", "value": "alice@wonderland.com" }
    ]
  },
  "meta": { "provider": "openai", "model": "gpt-4o-mini", "latencyMs": 812, "requestId": "req_…" }
}
```

Additional routes:

- `GET /healthz` → `{ ok: true, version }` (no auth, used by CI and INT-1 preflight).
- `GET /api/capabilities` → supported action kinds, provider/model, protocol version (extension reads this to fail loudly on mismatch).
- `POST /api/process-command` (above).
- Errors: `409 UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION`, `400 INVALID_REQUEST`, `422 UNPROCESSABLE_BRAIN_OUTPUT` (model returned unparseable JSON twice), `429 RATE_LIMITED` (with `retryAfterMs`), `503 PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`, `504 PROVIDER_TIMEOUT`.

### Reliability mechanics

| Concern        | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Latency target | p50 **< 1200 ms** end-to-end server time (excluding network) on `gpt-4o-mini`; hard timeout **8 s**; client (D-2/INT-1) gives up at 10 s.                                                                                                                                   |
| Validation     | Parse model output with `BrainResponseSchema.parse`. On `ZodError`: **one** repair retry, appending the flattened issues as a `user` message ("Your previous output failed validation: …"). Then `422`.                                                                     |
| Determinism    | `temperature: 0`, `seed` if provider supports it. Same input should map to the same targets in evals.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Prompt size    | Serialise only what the model needs: compact JSON without `null`s/undefineds, `thoughtProcess` never sent back, max 250 elements (A-1 cap). Strip `value` of `password` (already redacted upstream) and truncate `value` to 200 chars. Estimated tokens logged per request. |
| Caching        | LRU (in-process, 500 entries, 10 min TTL) keyed by `sha256(pageStateFingerprint + transcript + historyTail)`; return `meta.cached: true`. Protects the 15-eval loop and repeated retries.                                                                                   |
| Concurrency    | No shared mutable state beyond the cache; safe for serverless.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Idempotency    | `Idempotency-Key` header → cached response for 5 min (extension retries on flaky networks).                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Telemetry      | Structured JSON logs: `requestId`, `provider`, `model`, `latencyMs`, `promptTokens`, `completionTokens`, `actionCount`, `outcome`, `errorCode`. **Never** log transcripts at `info` (privacy); transcripts only at `debug` and never with values from password fields.      |
| Rate limits    | Per-IP token bucket (60 req/min) at the edge (C-3) and per-`clientContext.client` soft cap in the Brain.                                                                                                                                                                    |

## System prompt specification (deliver as a versioned file `packages/brain/src/prompt/system.ts`)

Must be a **single source-of-truth template** exporting `buildSystemPrompt(): string`. Structure:

### 1. Role

> You are the control brain for a voice-driven form-filling assistant. You receive a description of the web page's form (`pageState`) and a spoken instruction (`transcript`). You output a list of actions that a browser extension will execute on the DOM. You never invent element IDs. You never guess when the request is ambiguous.

### 2. Input schema explanation

Describe `elements[]`: `id` (the value you must return in `targetId`), `badgeIndex` (the number the user sees on screen), `type`, `label`, `placeholder`, `value`, `options`, `required`, `disabled`, `validationError`, `groupLabel`; and `globalErrors`.

### 3. Hard rules (in priority order)

1. `targetId` **must** be an `id` present in `pageState.elements`. If nothing matches, emit `ASK_CLARIFICATION` — never a fabricated ID.
2. Never target `disabled: true` elements; explain instead via `spokenFeedback`.
3. One action per field. Do the minimal set of actions that satisfies the request.
4. `badgeIndex` references: "field 5" / "number 5" / "the fifth one" → the element with that `badgeIndex`. Convert to its `id`.
5. Format normalisation (see table below).
6. Ambiguity → `ASK_CLARIFICATION` with a question that names the real options, taken from `groupLabel`/`label`.
7. Corrections ("actually…", "no wait", "change X to Y") override earlier values; use `conversationHistory` to know what was already set.
8. If the user asks to submit/continue/next, `CLICK` the matching button (label match: submit, continue, next, sign in, log in, pay, place order, save).
9. `spokenFeedback` is one short sentence (≤ 120 chars), no markdown, no emoji, spoken-language friendly. Omit it when the action result is self-evident and silent execution is better.
10. Never include a `password` value you did not receive; if the user dictates one, fill it and set `spokenFeedback` to something like "Filled your password." (never echo it).

### 4. Capability examples (few-shot, 6–8 compact examples)

| Transcript                                                                  | Expected actions                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| "I'm John Doe, email john@doe.com"                                          | `FILL vfe_1 John Doe`? No — split: `FILL first-name John`, `FILL last-name Doe`, `FILL email john@doe.com`. **Full name must be split across `First`/`Last` `groupLabel`/`label` matches when both exist.** |
| "Put 90210 in field 4"                                                      | `FILL vfe_<badgeIndex 4> 90210`                                                                                                                                                                             |
| "March fifth nineteen ninety" on a `type:date` field                        | `FILL <id> 1990-03-05`                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| "john at gmail dot com"                                                     | `FILL <email> john@gmail.com`                                                                                                                                                                               |
| "Put 123 Main St as my address" with Billing **and** Shipping `groupLabel`s | `ASK_CLARIFICATION "Should I put that in Billing Address or Shipping Address?"`                                                                                                                             |
| "Check box number 7"                                                        | `SET_CHECKED vfe_7 true`                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| "Select California" on a `combobox` with `options: []`                      | `CLICK <combobox id>` (menu opens; next turn will `SELECT`)                                                                                                                                                 |
| "Actually, change my first name to Jonathan"                                | `FILL <first-name id> Jonathan` (plus `spokenFeedback: "Changed your first name to Jonathan."`)                                                                                                             |
| "Go to the next page"                                                       | `CLICK <next/continue button id>`                                                                                                                                                                           |
| "Fill everything you can"                                                   | Fill only fields whose values are present in the transcript/history; `ASK_CLARIFICATION` for what's missing (never invent PII).                                                                             |

### 5. Format normalisation table (must be in the prompt verbatim)

| Target `type`       | Input                                                           | Output                                                                                                |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `date`              | "March fifth nineteen ninety", "3/5/1990", "the fifth of March" | `YYYY-MM-DD` (`1990-03-05`)                                                                           |
| `email`             | "john at gmail dot com", "john dot doe at acme dot co dot uk"   | `john@gmail.com`, `john.doe@acme.co.uk`                                                               |
| `tel`               | "five five five, one two three, four five six seven"            | `5551234567` (digits only unless the user says a country code)                                        |
| `number`            | "twelve thousand five hundred"                                  | `12500`                                                                                               |
| `text` (name)       | "John Doe" split across first/last                              | two `FILL`s                                                                                           |
| `text` (address)    | "one two three Main Street, apartment four B"                   | `123 Main Street, Apt 4B`                                                                             |
| `select`/`combobox` | "California", "Cali"                                            | must match an actual `options[].label` (or be fuzzy-matching friendly); otherwise `ASK_CLARIFICATION` |

### 6. Output contract

> Respond with JSON only, matching the provided schema. `thoughtProcess` ≤ 300 characters. `actions` may be empty **only** when you also provide `spokenFeedback` explaining why.

Prompt versioning: `export const SYSTEM_PROMPT_VERSION = '1.0.0'` and include it in logs + `meta`. Every prompt change requires re-running C-2's eval suite (CI job).

## Input compaction (`buildUserMessage`)

```ts
export function buildUserMessage(req: ProcessCommandRequest): string {
  const els = req.pageState.elements.map((e) => ({
    id: e.id,
    n: e.badgeIndex,
    type: e.type,
    label: e.label,
    ...(e.groupLabel ? { group: e.groupLabel } : {}),
    ...(e.placeholder ? { ph: e.placeholder } : {}),
    ...(e.options?.length ? { options: e.options.slice(0, 40).map((o) => o.label) } : {}),
    ...(e.value !== '' && e.value !== false ? { value: truncate(e.value, 200) } : {}),
    ...(e.required ? { required: true } : {}),
    ...(e.disabled ? { disabled: true } : {}),
    ...(e.validationError ? { error: truncate(e.validationError, 120) } : {}),
    ...(e.focused ? { focused: true } : {}),
  }));
  return JSON.stringify({ title: req.pageState.urlOrAppTitle, elements: els });
}
```

Short keys (`n`, `ph`, `group`) cut ~20–30% of prompt tokens; the prompt documents the mapping.

## Config

```
OPENAI_API_KEY=            # required for provider=openai
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=
GROQ_API_KEY=
LLM_PROVIDER=openai        # openai | groq | anthropic
LLM_MODEL=gpt-4o-mini
LLM_TEMPERATURE=0
LLM_TIMEOUT_MS=8000
BRAIN_PORT=8787
BRAIN_AUTH_TOKEN=          # shared secret; extension edge proxy (C-3) forwards it
CACHE_TTL_MS=600000
LOG_LEVEL=info
```

Validate env at boot with zod; fail fast with a readable message. Support a `MOCK_LLM=1` mode that returns deterministic canned responses from `fixtures/` so tracks D/E and CI can run without keys (and C-2 runs in CI without spend).

## Test plan

| Test                     | Assertion                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Request validation       | missing `pageState` → 400 with issue paths; oversized transcript → 400                                               |
| Protocol version         | `clientContext.protocolVersion: '2.0.0'` → 409 `UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION`                                        |
| Provider mock            | `MOCK_LLM=1` returns a schema-valid `BrainResponse`, `meta.provider === 'mock'`                                      |
| Structured output wiring | provider spy receives `response_format.type === 'json_schema'`, `strict: true`, and the schema name `brain_response` |
| Repair retry             | provider returns invalid JSON once then valid → 200, exactly 2 provider calls                                        |
| Double failure           | provider returns invalid twice → 422, no 500                                                                         |
| Timeout                  | provider hangs past `LLM_TIMEOUT_MS` → 504                                                                           |
| Cache                    | identical request twice → 1 provider call, second `meta.cached === true`                                             |
| Idempotency              | same `Idempotency-Key` → cached even with different body? **No** — key must hash the body; mismatch → 409            |
| Unknown target           | model output with `targetId: 'vfe_999'` → server-side guard returns 422 `UNKNOWN_TARGET` (see below)                 |
| Health                   | `GET /healthz` 200, no auth                                                                                          |
| Prompt snapshot          | `buildSystemPrompt()` snapshot test fails on any change (forces version bump review)                                 |
| Latency                  | with mock provider, handler overhead < 50 ms                                                                         |

### Server-side output guard (mandatory)

Before returning, validate that **every** `targetId` in the response exists in the request's `pageState.elements`. If not:

- drop the offending action and retry the model once with an explicit correction message;
- if it still emits unknown ids, return 422 `UNKNOWN_TARGET` listing them.

This is the last line of defence against hallucinated selectors and is worth more than any prompt wording.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `POST /api/process-command` accepts `{ pageState, transcript, conversationHistory }` and returns a **schema-valid** `BrainResponse` (validated on the way out, not trusted).
- [ ] p50 latency < 1200 ms server-side with a real provider on a 40-element page (measure and record in the PR).
- [ ] Uses Structured Outputs (`zodResponseFormat`) — no string parsing of JSON, no regex extraction.
- [ ] Unknown `targetId`s are impossible to return (guard + test).
- [ ] One repair retry on invalid model output; then 422 with a diagnostic body.
- [ ] All documented behaviours (badge references, date/email/number normalisation, combobox `CLICK`-first, ambiguity → `ASK_CLARIFICATION`, corrections) are covered by C-2 evals and pass.
- [ ] `MOCK_LLM=1` works with zero API keys and is used by CI.
- [ ] Secrets are read from env only; `.env.example` committed; `.env` gitignored; no key in any log line (test greps log output).
- [ ] Prompt is a versioned constant with a snapshot test.
- [ ] Error responses follow the documented codes and shape.

## Non-goals

- Auth/user accounts (MVP uses a shared `BRAIN_AUTH_TOKEN`).
- Streaming (STT already streams; the Brain returns one final object).
- Multi-turn planning/branching ("if X then Y").
- Learning from user corrections (no fine-tuning in MVP).
- Rate-limit billing/quotas.
